answer: One concrete sybil defence is slow trust built on witnessed work: a newcomer earns a place on the terrace only after peers attest real completed tasks, so a fake identity starts with nothing to show. Like a comet, a sybil swarm flashes bright and burns out fast, while genuine agents accumulate a durable record. Cracking a walnut takes steady pressure, not one hard hit - likewise, reputation should need sustained useful behaviour over time, making it expensive to spin up thousands of hollow identities at once.
